entry.summary:
Source: @mohsenhesammazaheri

#New_Book_Releases_ArmaOn the eve of the 47th anniversary of Ayatollah Taleghani's passing, published:📔Payk-e Aftab📔A Study of the Record and Intellectual Legacy of Ayatollah Seyyed Mahmoud Taleghani(Third Edition)✍️ Mohammad EsfandiariFirst printing — Shahrivar 1405Roqai — 497 pagesThis book is a study of the era, life, thoughts, and works of Ayatollah Taleghani; a rare man who did not live for himself, never became confined to his own limitations, and devoted the capital of his life to the revival of humanity and humaneness. Among figures outside the religious sphere, Taleghani resembled Socrates and Gandhi. In epistemology, like Socrates, he believed that we know less than we think we do, and therefore we must learn from one another through dialogue, questioning, and answering. But in politics, he was like Gandhi; as hard as stone against the enemy and as soft as silk with a friend. In the two halves of the 20th century, two spiritual-political figures shone, each adorning humanity: Gandhi and Taleghani. The world knew and honored Gandhi, but alas, it did not know Taleghani and remained deprived. His compatriots, too, who found him in the heat of the revolution, lost him in the storm of subsequent events.Distribution: QoqnoosOnline purchase: IranKetab and CBook websites@nashre_arma

entry.title: [mohsenhesammazaheri] These days, insulting Shariati and other religious intellectuals is, of course,…
entry.summary:
Source: @mohsenhesammazaheri

These days, insulting Shariati and other religious intellectuals is, of course, in vogue, and anyone who comes along hurls insults at them. But one must be fair: regarding the Holy Prophet, at least in Persian and in the contemporary era, no work has yet been written that matches "Muhammad, the Seal of the Prophets," and especially Shariati's essay in it titled "The Face of Muhammad." My knowledge of and devotion to the Prophet I owe to this book and to Shariati's "Islamology"; just as my interest in Quranic studies I owe to Engineer Bazargan and his "The Evolution of the Quran." @mohsenhesammazaheri
